==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Two-aspect-signal ES692.jpg|thumb|150px|Two-[[aspect]] railway signal]]

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|signall}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{der|en|fro|segnal}}, {{m|fro|seignal}} or {{der|en|la-med|signāle}}; noun use of the neuter of {{der|en|la-lat|signālis}}, from {{der|en|la|signum}}; verb use from 1805, as a shortened from ''[[signalize]]'' (1650s). {{doublet|en|signum|sign}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|sĭgʹnəl}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈsɪɡnəl/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-signal.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪɡnəl|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|sig|nal}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A sequence of states representing an encoded message in a communication channel.
# Any variation of a quantity or change in an entity over time that conveys information upon detection.
# A [[sign]] made to give notice of some occurrence, command, or danger, or to indicate the start of a concerted action.
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=V|passage=All obeyed / The wonted '''signal''' and superior voice / Of this great potentate.|year=1873}}
# An on-off light, [[semaphore]], or other device used to give an indication to another person.
## A [[railway signal]].
# {{lb|en|of a radio, TV, telephone, internet, etc.}} An [[electromagnetic]] action, normally a [[voltage]] that is a function of time, that conveys the information of the radio or TV program or of communication with another party.
#: {{ux|en|My mobile phone can't get a '''signal''' in the railway station.}}
# An action, change or process done to convey information and thus reduce uncertainty.
# A [[token]]; an [[indication]]; a [[foreshadowing]]; a [[sign]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|V|iii|passage=The weary sun {{...}} / Gives '''signal''' of a goodly day to-morrow.}}
#* {{RQ:Defoe Plague Year|passage=There was not the least '''signal''' of the calamity to be seen.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|title=Hurtz So Bad|album={{w|Hit Parade (Róisín Murphy album)|Hit Parade}}|author=w:Róisín Murphy|year=2023|passage=Did I get it wrong all along? / You were sending '''signals''' / You sent certain '''signals''' to me}}
# {{U|useful}} [[information]], as opposed to [[noise]].
#: {{ant|en|noise}}
# {{lb|en|computing|Unix}} A simple [[interprocess]] [[communication]] used to [[notify]] a [[process]] or [[thread]] of an occurrence.
# {{lb|en|biochemistry}} A [[signalling]] [[interaction]] between [[cell]]s.

===Verb===
{{en-verb|+l}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[indicate]]; to [[convey]] or [[communicate]] by a signal.
#: {{hypo|en|signpost|telegraph}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''signalled''' my [[acquiescence]] with a nod.}}
#: {{ux|en|He whistled to '''signal''' that we should stop.}}
#: {{ux|en|My arms wheeled frantically in the air as I tried to '''signal''' for help.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Andy Nottenkamper|title=A Rule Not Followed
|passage=I '''signaled''' for our waiter and ordered two Glenlivets, the only single malt they had behind the bar.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2025-04-21|author=Peter Stanford|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/apr/21/pope-francis-obituary|title=Pope Francis obituary|passage=The break with tradition that Francis, who has died aged 88 after suffering from double pneumonia, represented even managed to trump the shock value of the resignation of Benedict, who was the first pope for 600 years to take that option rather than die in office. Immediately, Bergoglio '''signalled''' unambiguously that he intended to be a different kind of pope, one for the 21st century.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250726023852/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/apr/21/pope-francis-obituary}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To communicate with (a person or system) by a signal.
#: {{ux|en|Seeing the flames, he ran to the control room and '''signalled''' headquarters.}}
